identification: Two raw live-edge slabs, one tall narrow with a knot hole and split, one shorter, wide, reddish-orange brown with darker grain. Colour looks warmer than typical pale yellow Huon pine, so ID is doubtful (could be myrtle, blackwood or similar). Gowans sells hundreds of lots titled '2 SLABS OF HUON PINE' with the same look.

viewing_check: Smell and cut/scratch a clean spot: genuine Huon pine has a strong sweet oil scent and pale yellow-gold colour with fine bird's-eye or tight growth rings. Note length, width and thickness, depth of the split and knot hole, and whether the wood is dry and sound.
